title: Rotate Image
problemStatement:
You are given an n x n 2D matrix representing an image, rotate the image by 90 degrees (clockwise).

You have to rotate the image in-place, which means you have to modify the input 2D matrix directly. DO NOT allocate another 2D matrix and do the rotation.

Example 1:

Input: matrix = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]
Output: [[7,4,1],[8,5,2],[9,6,3]]

Example 2:

Input: matrix = [[5,1,9,11],[2,4,8,10],[13,3,6,7],[15,14,12,16]]
Output: [[15,13,2,5],[14,3,4,1],[12,6,8,9],[16,7,10,11]]

Constraints:

- n == matrix.length == matrix[i].length

- 1 <= n <= 20

- -1000 <= matrix[i][j] <= 1000

latestSubmission.code:
class Solution:
    def rotate(self, matrix: List[List[int]]) -> None:
        """
        brute-force
        -- j --
        (0,0)      (0,3)
    |   [_ , _ , _ , _]
    i   [_ , _ , _ , _]
    |   [_ , _ , _ , _]
        (3,0)      (3,3)

        Ater rotate 90 degree clockwise
        -- i --
        (3,0)      (0,0)
        [_ , _ , _ , _]     |
        [_ , _ , _ , _]     j
        [_ , _ , _ , _]     |
        (3,3)      (0,3)

        new row = old col
        new col = n - 1 - old row

        idea is to do 2 nested loops, outer loop is to go ring by ring, the inner loop is to rotate the edge
        """
        n = len(matrix)
        # n // 2 is the number of layerd ring we have to rotate (floor division)
        # for case where n % 2 == 1, matrix will have the 1 central cell where we skip because we don't need to rotate that
        for i in range(n // 2):
            # here j start at i and stop before n - i - 1
            # because inner rings will have less element than the outer ring
            for j in range(i, n - i - 1):
                matrix[i][j], matrix[j][n-1-i], matrix[n-1-i][n-1-j], matrix[n-1-j][i] = matrix[n-1-j][i], matrix[i][j], matrix[j][n-1-i], matrix[n-1-i][n-1-j]
